sentence: This project studies how growth hormone protects female liver cells from fat buildup and damage, and how it changes their contact with other cells.
This project builds a platform that lets cell therapy developers quickly check whether cells used for therapeutic products carry cancer-causing mutations.
This project tests whether cerium oxide nanoparticles can help with both imaging and treatment of inflammatory bowel disease.
This project studies how angiotensin converting enzyme changes the metabolism of macrophages and neutrophils and so improves how these immune cells work.
This project studies how extracellular vesicles affect mitochondria in brain microvascular endothelial cells and tests whether stem cell-derived vesicles help in infected humanized mice.
This project studies what controls the movement of mesothelial cells and how these cells help organs form and stay healthy.
This project studies how tissue-engineered vascular grafts change over time in male, female, and post-menopausal female rats, and what role estrogen plays.
This project studies how Mycobacterium tuberculosis uses cyclic AMP signaling to adapt to host cells and survive antibiotics, including the effect of naturally occurring mutations.
This project tries to find what controls the size and shape of the cell nucleus and how these features affect development, cell differentiation, and cancer.
This project builds a mouse model to test drugs combined with T-cell directed treatments for myeloma, which patients often relapse from.
This project studies how neutrophil elastase, related proteases, and their substrates disrupt blood cell production in congenital neutropenia, using human stem cell models.
This project tests whether remote ischemic preconditioning protects the kidneys from contrast-associated injury in Veterans with congestive heart failure who cannot tolerate intravenous fluid.
This project builds sample delivery methods that control the sample environment precisely, so enzyme reactions can be studied with an X-ray free electron laser.
This project supports a center that coordinates and adds value to HIV research programs and works toward preventing and treating HIV.
This project studies how reactive aldehydes that build up in cancers and age-related diseases damage proteins and cause genome instability.
This project builds T cell immunotherapies aimed at a leukemia surface marker and tests them together with menin inhibition to overcome treatment resistance in leukemia.
This project studies how histotripsy, which destroys tumors with high intensity ultrasound waves, triggers cell death events that lead to an immune response against tumors.
This project builds near-infrared imaging probes from silver nanoclusters and nucleic acid nanoparticles to help treat and diagnose ovarian cancer.
This project builds a computer method using deep learning to predict how long protein complexes with G-protein-coupled receptors last, and tests the predictions.
This project studies how brain circuits control shifts between sleep states in a mouse model of Parkinson's disease, which causes broken sleep.
